- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% relative to historical mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model should undercorrect upward momentum; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% to align with sentiment-driven bearish bias.
- After a price spike (e.g., > +3% from prior period), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply a 1–2% downward correction to prevent overreaction.
- Mean reversion is evident in 10–14 day horizons; if forecast exceeds 2 SD above recent 18-day mean, reduce by 1–3% to reflect reversion bias.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from negative to positive) triggers model lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and reduce upward bias by 0.5–1.0% until sentiment stabilizes.
